method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Civil Liability Act 2002 (WA) (No. 35 of 2002), compilation as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/mrdoc_49335.txt (legislation.wa.gov.au mrdoc 49335, retrieved 2026-09-07), with the s 9(3) formula from ../../registers/source-bundle/mrdoc_49335.formulas.md (transcribed by hand on 2026-10-21 from the authorised Word rendering of mrdoc 49335); no regulations or Gazette notices used: Amounts A, B and C for a year after 2002-03 and the average weekly earnings are inputs

checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: ss 3, 3A (which classes of damages the Act's Parts do not reach: intentional and sexual harm, motor vehicle (CTP), workers' compensation common-law claims against the employer, tobacco, aviation, asbestos and silica), 4 (indexing, rounded to $500), 5A, 5B, 5E-5J (recreational activities, risk warnings, waivers), 5K-5L (contributory negligence, intoxication), 5N-5P (obvious and inherent risks), 6, 9 (general damages threshold, the band to Amount C and the s 9(3) middle band), 10, 11 (loss of earnings capped at 3 x AWE), 12, 13 (gratuitous home care). Out: Parts 1B-1F, Part 1A Div 7, s 13A, Part 2 Divs 4-5, Parts 2A and 3.
lives: jake k044 (2029-04-12): a car door fractures his wrist on a delivery; no workers' compensation for a contractor; a CTP claim against the driver's insurer
